1.explanation:
The root of the problem lies in how highlight.js decides which character sequences count as keywords versus ordinary identifiers. In python.js:

• IDENT_RE (const IDENT_RE = /[\p{XID_Start}_]\p{XID_Continue}*/u) defines the full identifier pattern and correctly matches “_undef” as one token.  
• KEYWORDS (const KEYWORDS = { $pattern: /[A-Za-z]\w+|__\w+__/, keyword: RESERVED_WORDS, … }) provides the regex used to pull out potential keywords. Because its $pattern does not allow an underscore at the start, it splits “_undef” into two pieces under the hood and then matches “def” against the reserved‐words list, incorrectly marking it as a keyword.

To fix this, the $pattern for KEYWORDS must be broadened (for example to include leading underscores) so that “_undef” is never subdivided and its internal “def” cannot be reinterpreted as the standalone keyword.
1.bug_scenario:
In the Python snippet “foo = _undef
bar” the identifier “_undef” is being split so that the trailing “def” is treated as the Python keyword “def” (and gets the keyword highlight), even though it is part of a single identifier. The screenshot shows only the “def” in “_undef” wrapped in <span class="hljs-keyword">, which is incorrect.

2.explanation: The root of the problem lives in src/languages/python.js. IDENT_RE correctly defines what a valid Python identifier is (including leading underscores), but the keyword matcher (the KEYWORDS object) uses its own $pattern (/[A-Za-z]\w+|__\w+__/) that doesn’t allow a leading underscore. That mismatch lets “_undef” be broken at the ‘def’ substring and triggers the reserved-word styling. Additionally, compileKeywords in src/lib/compile_keywords.js assembles the final keyword lookup table from the raw lists—because compileKeywords never enforces word-boundary checks around keywords, it amplifies the split. Fixing this requires aligning the KEYWORDS.$pattern with IDENT_RE (so keywords only match full identifiers or are bounded by word breaks) and/or adjusting compileKeywords to respect the full identifier regex rather than matching substrings.
2.bug_scenario:
When highlighting this Python snippet in highlight.js v11.x+:

    foo = _undef
    bar

the identifier “_undef” gets split into “_un” (plain text) and “def” (highlighted as a Python keyword). In other words, the engine sees “_undef” as ending with the keyword “def” and incorrectly re-tokenizes it, so that “def” is styled as if it were the function-definition keyword.
